symptom: In an x86-64 image, the Linux i386 compatibility sequence `mov eax,1; mov ebx,0; int 0x80` remained `(*(code *)swi(0x80))();` even with `linuxsyscall on`, erasing the syscall number and status.
root_cause: The pass rejected every language whose default code address size was not four. Long-mode SLEIGH also normalizes `mov eax,imm32` into an eight-byte zero-extending COPY to RAX before this pre-SSA pass, so resolving only EAX would still fail to find the number.
decisions: Treat `int 0x80` in a 64-bit x86 language as Linux's i386 compatibility entry: i386 syscall numbers and EBX/ECX/EDX/ESI/EDI/EBP argument order, each represented by the low four-byte storage of the containing 64-bit register.

Resolve the complete RAX/RBX/RCX/RDX/RSI/RDI/RBP register records at their declared eight-byte widths, then retain their offsets with four-byte parameter and result types. This is a bounded language probe, not permissive sub-register lookup.

Accept only an exact constant COPY to the four-byte number storage or, in long mode only, the exact eight-byte RAX storage emitted by SLEIGH. Source and destination widths must match; partial, mismatched, computed, overlapping, and non-x86 writes remain refusals.
Keep the structural `swi(0x80)` matcher and rewrite unchanged. Native x86-64 `SYSCALL` remains owned by `x64syscall`, so linuxsyscall cannot reinterpret native syscall number 1 as i386 exit.
The `kuna-base/src/xml.rs` delta is only the generated corpus guard changing from 274 to 275 because one stage file was added; it contains no production or register-resolution logic.
